cohorts.subjects: Living adults: 100 'healthy volunteers' who had a lumbar spine CT at the Department of Health Examination of Zhengzhou Orthopedic Hospital, Henan, China, between September 2023 and September 2025, enrolled retrospectively; called healthy Chinese adults, no further ethnicity printed. Inclusion: age 20 to 70, a standard lumbar spine CT, no lumbar surgery or trauma. Exclusion: vertebral fracture on CT by a semiquantitative method, congenital vertebral deformity or acquired short vertebral body, spinal metal implants, drugs or diseases affecting bone metabolism, adult degenerative scoliosis or severe osteophytosis. No count of screened or excluded people. Level identification and transitional vertebrae are not mentioned.
cohorts.n_units: 500 vertebral bodies, L1 to L5 of 100 people (Inference: no missing levels are reported; n per level is not printed)
cohorts.ages: 20 to 70 years; Table 1 gives five decade bands of 20 people each, band means 25.1 +/- 3.4 to 65.4 +/- 2.3 years
cohorts.sexes: 50 male and 50 female by the Abstract and Results text; Table 1 columns sum to 46 male and 54 female; no sex-stratified values
cohorts.page: p. 1 (PDF 1); p. 2 to 3 (PDF 2 to 3); p. 4 to 5 (PDF 4 to 5); p. 8 (PDF 8)

cohorts.subjects: CT images of unnamed subjects used to show how the measures were taken: Figure 1 two sagittal MPR panels with caliper readouts, Figure 3 one sagittal and twelve axial slices with ROI software readouts. The paper does not say whose scans or which levels they are. Inference: probably members of the main cohort, but this is not stated, so their values are kept apart.
cohorts.n_units: Figure 1: one lumbar body per panel (2 panels); Figure 3: 3 sagittal ROIs and 12 axial ROIs (one per quadrant at each third); level not stated

cohorts.subjects: Another study quoted for comparison: an anatomical study of dried lumbar vertebrae in a Nepalese population (Shrestha 2022; its reference describes a cross-sectional study of specimens in a medical college anatomy department). Its reference title names a canal-body ratio study; which width is quoted (body or end-plate, upper or lower) is not said.

Another study quoted for comparison: 168 healthy men whose lumbar BMD fell from L1 to L4 in every age group (Liu et al. 2005, a Chinese gerontology journal by its reference). Only the count is quoted.

quoted from Elarjani et al. 2021 (World Neurosurg): a mean lumbar CT value threshold for augmentation; no subjects described

techniques.instrument: Siemens Somatom Definition 64 AS+ spiral CT as printed; acquisition slice 3.0 mm, collimation 128 x 0.6 mm, pitch 0.8, scan angle 0 deg, 120 kV, no contrast; reconstructed at 1 mm thickness and 1 mm interval, kernel B60s sharp, bone window; MPR on a syngo MMWP VE36A workstation; tube current, field of view and pixel spacing not printed
techniques.how: Seven body parameters of L1 to L5 on CT MPR: the list of the seven opens by putting them on mid-sagittal images, and a later sentence says mid-sagittal and mid-coronal planes, so no parameter is given a plane of its own (Inference: widths on the mid-coronal, the rest mid-sagittal): anterior, middle and posterior body heights from the superior to the inferior endplate at its front edge, midpoint and back edge; superior and inferior endplate widths between the outermost lateral edges of each endplate; cortical thickness of the superior endplate measured vertically in its anterior and posterior thirds. Figure 1B draws the widths on a sagittal slice (Inference: Table 2 widths of 42 to 52 mm fit a mediolateral span, not the 30 mm AP span drawn).
techniques.magnification: CT in true scale; no magnification correction applies (not discussed)
techniques.observers: One trained observer (the first author), blinded to subject characteristics; each parameter measured three times and averaged; intra-observer ICC > 0.90 for all parameters on 20 random vertebrae re-measured after 2 weeks; inter-observer reliability not evaluated

techniques.instrument: the same CT, reconstruction and workstation as ct_mpr_morphometry; same scanner, kernel and 120 kV for every subject, no contrast; no phantom calibration
techniques.how: After Banse et al. 2001: each body split into upper, middle and lower thirds on the sagittal plane and, on an axial slice in each third, into left anterior, right anterior, left posterior and right posterior quadrants, 15 regions per body; a circular or elliptical ROI of about 1 cm2 in the cancellous bone of each, avoiding cortex, basivertebral foramen, osteophytes and calcification; mean HU in the ROI, three measurements averaged. Which axial slice in each third is not stated; Figure 3 shows rectangular ROIs of about 85 to 211 mm2 by its readouts. Left and right convention (image or patient) not stated.
techniques.magnification: not applicable (attenuation values in HU); no phantom or DXA calibration
techniques.observers: Not stated for HU beyond three repeats per region. Inference: the same single observer; the ICC statement sits in the morphology section and may not cover HU.

techniques.modality: dry bone (Inference from the reference title)

within_paper: One cohort of 100 people: Tables 1 to 6, Figure 4 and the text values are all of the same 100 subjects and the same 500 bodies, measured on the same scans; morphometry (Table 2) and HU (Tables 3 to 6) are two measurement sets on the same bodies, and Table 3 (sagittal thirds) and Tables 4 to 6 (axial quadrants) are two ROI schemes on the same bodies (p. 3 to 7 (PDF 3 to 7)). Figure 4 replots Table 3 (p. 6 (PDF 6)). The example images of Figures 1 and 3 are of unnamed subjects whose membership in the cohort is not stated (p. 3 to 4 (PDF 3 to 4)). Inference: none of the 42 listed studies shares subjects; arockiaraj2025, moncadahabib2025, tan2004 and kunkel2011 are cited only as background (p. 2 and p. 6 (PDF 2, 6)).
